# How a root tip makes a root longer

<!-- STEP id="new-cells" -->
## New cells at the tip

The very end of a root is covered by a small protective cap. Just behind this cap is a group of small cells that keep dividing. This is the apical meristem, and each division adds new cells there.

<!-- STEP id="lengthen" -->
## Cells behind it grow longer

As more cells are made, the older new cells are left a little behind the tip. These cells then grow longer, so the root becomes longer and the tip is pushed deeper. Further back from the tip, the cells stop growing longer.

<!-- STEP id="ink-marks" -->
## A classic test with ink marks

In a classic experiment, ink marks are drawn at equal gaps along a young root, starting at the tip. After a day or two, only the marks near the tip have moved apart. The marks further back still have the same gaps between them.

**A root grows longer only near its tip: new cells are made at the tip, and the cells just behind it grow longer.**
